intended_object: A left rigid (left autonomous) monoidal category: a monoidal category in which every object has a left dual. The name, the companion `RightRigidCategory`, `RigidCategory` (which extends both) and the module documentation all point to this.
explanation:
The class asks for a `HasLeftDual X` instance for every object `X`. That instance is an object `ᘁX` together with an `ExactPairing (ᘁX) X`, i.e. evaluation and coevaluation maps satisfying the zigzag (triangle) identities. This is exactly "every object has a left dual", in Mathlib's own left/right convention. Conventions for which dual counts as "left" differ between authors, but Mathlib uses its convention consistently. The library depends on this choice: `monoidalClosedOfLeftRigidCategory` builds a closed structure with internal hom `ᘁX ⊗ Y`, which needs exactly a pairing `ExactPairing (ᘁX) X`.

The docstring says "every object has a right dual". This is an obvious copy-paste of the `RightRigidCategory` docstring on the line just above. The name, the field (`leftDual : ∀ X, HasLeftDual X`) and every use of the class show that left duals are meant. So the docstring has a typo, but the definition is right.

The generality is natural: any category with any monoidal structure. There is no other Mathlib definition of this notion.
